angle: AI roadmaps depend on the physical grid: transformer supply crunch changes timelines and risk
sourceTitle: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply
linkedinPost:
Your AI roadmap has a hidden dependency: steel, copper, and lead times.

McKinsey notes we’re in a transformer supercycle — demand up, supply constrained, changing decisions across the value chain. You feel this when the data center you planned for Q2 slips because the substation can’t expand.

My take: treat power and grid gear like critical-path software dependencies. Bake them into your risk register and stage-gate AI bets around them.

Three tactics I’ve seen work:

- Portfolio thinking: mix "compute-light" wins (RAG on existing infra, process automation) with "compute-heavy" bets to keep value flowing.

- Location arbitrage: partner with facilities teams early; sometimes the fastest AI value is where power is available, not where the team sits.

- Contract design: tie vendor SLAs and milestones to facilities readiness, not just model delivery.

If your AI strategy assumes infinite power and instant hookups, it’s not a strategy — it’s a hope.

Where does your AI plan depend on physical infrastructure you don’t control? #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI #DigitalTransformation
